A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Normal Space|normal space]], $A \subseteq X$ [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed]] and $f: A \to \closedint {-1} 1$ [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Topology)|continuous]].
Then $f$ extends to a continuous $F: X \to \closedint {-1} 1$.

B_source.statement:
Let $X$ be normal and $E$, $F$ disjoint closed sets.
Then there is a continuous $h: X \to \closedint 0 1$ with $h = 0$ on $E$ and $h = 1$ on $F$.

substitutions.a single Urysohn function: a sequence of corrections h_n of geometrically shrinking size

object_map.reformulation: Extend f approximately, with error reduced by a factor 2/3 at each step, and sum the geometric series of corrections.

validity_conditions: A must be closed, so that sets closed in A are closed in X.
Uniform convergence of the series preserves continuity.
proof_plan:
Let $g: A \to \closedint {-c} c$ be continuous.
The sets $\set {g \le -c / 3}$ and $\set {g \ge c / 3}$ are disjoint and closed in $X$.
By the source result there is continuous $h: X \to \closedint {-c / 3} {c / 3}$ equal to $-c / 3$ on the first and $c / 3$ on the second, and then $\size {g - h} \le \dfrac {2 c} 3$ on $A$.

Apply this to $g_0 = f$ with $c = 1$, then to $g_1 = f - h_0$ with $c = \dfrac 2 3$, and so on.
This gives $h_n$ with $\size {h_n} \le \dfrac 1 3 \paren {\dfrac 2 3}^n$ and $\size {f - \sum_{k \le n} h_k} \le \paren {\dfrac 2 3}^{n + 1}$ on $A$.
By the [[Weierstrass M-Test]], $F = \displaystyle \sum_k h_k$ converges uniformly, so is continuous, with $\size F \le \displaystyle \sum_n \frac 1 3 \paren {\frac 2 3}^n = 1$.
